### 4.1 Transfer within the same data distribution
［#26］
As a first test of whether winning tickets generalize, we investigate the simplest form of transfer: generalization across samples drawn from the same data distribution. To measure this, we divided

［#28］
**Figure 2:** Transferring winning tickets within the same data distribution. CIFAR-10 was divided into two halves ("10a" and "10b"), each of which contained 25,000 total examples with 2,500 images per class. Winning tickets generated using CIFAR-10a generalized well to CIFAR-10b for both VGG19 (a) and ResNet50 (b). Error bars represent mean ± standard deviation across six random seeds.

related_claims.content: A winning ticket discovered on CIFAR-10a (a subset of the CIFAR-10 dataset containing 25,000 training images with 2,500 images per class), transfers to a disjoint subset CIFAR-10b from the same data distribution and improves training on that held-out subset relative to random sparse initializations.

claims.A: winning tickets generated using CIFAR-10a for VGG19 and ResNet50
claims.S: transfer within the same data distribution (CIFAR-10 divided into two halves, '10a' and '10b')
claims.U: mean ± standard deviation across six random seeds
claims.content: Under transfer within the same data distribution (CIFAR-10 divided into two halves, '10a' and '10b'), winning tickets generated using CIFAR-10a for VGG19 and ResNet50 on generalization to CIFAR-10b showed to be good; uncertainty: mean ± standard deviation across six random seeds.
